rules.description: Applications may not depend directly on sibling applications
rules.remediation: Move shared behavior behind a package/domain boundary and depend on that public contract.

rules.description: Browser-facing application and UI modules may not import Node.js core modules
rules.remediation: Move Node-only behavior to a build/server adapter or replace it with a browser platform API.

rules.description: Production JavaScript and TypeScript dependency cycles are forbidden
rules.remediation: Break the cycle by extracting a lower-level contract or reversing the dependency direction.

rules.description: Feature/domain packages may not reach into a sibling feature/domain implementation
rules.remediation: Integrate through a foundational/shared package or an explicit public domain contract.

rules.description: Production source may not import generated, coverage, build, or distribution internals
rules.remediation: Depend on canonical source or a declared package export instead of generated internals.
Remove dead code or document and configure the module as an intentional entry point.

rules.description: Applications may not bypass package public exports to import package source internals
rules.remediation: Import the package public entry point/export map instead of a source-internal module.

rules.description: Reusable packages may not depend on applications
rules.remediation: Invert the dependency so applications compose packages, never the reverse.

rules.description: Production modules may not depend on tests, specs, or fixtures
rules.remediation: Move reusable test helpers behind a production-safe support package or keep the dependency test-only.

rules.description: Every analyzed dependency must resolve deterministically
rules.remediation: Correct the import path, package export, alias configuration, or missing dependency declaration.
